classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the repeated colour and directly explain the taught rule that each distinct set element is listed once.

content.prompt:
$A=\{\text{red},\text{white},\text{blue}\}$, $B=\{\text{green},\text{red},\text{yellow},\text{black}\}$.

Explain why, when listing the elements of $A\cup B$, we should not write $\{\text{red},\text{white},\text{blue},\text{green},\text{red},\text{yellow},\text{black}\}$.

answer.short: Red is repeated. Each distinct element should be listed only once.
answer.worked:
Red belongs to both $A$ and $B$, but it is included only once when listing the union.

$A\cup B=\{\text{red},\text{white},\text{blue},\text{green},\text{yellow},\text{black}\}$.
